title: Georgian shoti bread
subtitle: canoe-shaped Georgian yeasted flatbread baked at very high heat
excerpt: Shoti is a traditional Georgian yeasted flatbread with a distinctive long, canoe shape and a thin, crisp crust with a hollow interior. It is traditionally baked in a tone, a clay oven in the ground, by pressing the shaped dough onto the inner wall of the oven. The home oven version is baked on a preheated tray or stone at maximum heat. The bread is hollow inside with a crackling crust.
sourceNotes: Shoti is a Georgian national bread documented in Georgian cookery from at least the sixteenth century. It is baked in a tone oven and is a staple bread across Georgia. The word shoti refers specifically to the long, pointed canoe shape.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze baked shoti on the day of baking. Reheat in a hot oven for 5 minutes from frozen.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best eaten within an hour of baking. The crust softens as it cools and is not restorable fully.
recipe.temperatureNote: fan 230 degrees C / gas 9, or as high as the oven goes

content.text: Shoti is a long, canoe-shaped Georgian flatbread with pointed ends and a hollow interior. The dough is relatively wet, which creates the open crumb and the thin, blistered crust. Shaping takes practice; the bread is stretched long and thin with both hands before the ends are twisted and pinched to points. Baking on a preheated tray at maximum oven heat is the critical step.

Combine the flour, instant yeast, salt, and sugar. Add the warm water and mix until a dough forms. Knead for 8 to 10 minutes until smooth. The dough will be wetter than a standard bread dough and quite extensible. Cover and leave to rise for 90 minutes until doubled.
Place two heavy baking trays in the oven. Heat to 250 degrees C (fan 230 degrees C / gas 9), or as high as your oven goes, for at least 30 minutes.

Divide the dough in half. Working with lightly floured hands, gently stretch each piece into a long oval about 40 cm long and 15 cm wide. The dough should be about 1 cm thick in the centre. Pinch and twist the two ends to form sharp points. Place on sheets of baking paper.
Leave to rest uncovered for 20 to 30 minutes while the oven reaches full temperature.

Slide the shoti on their baking paper onto the hot trays. Bake for 15 to 20 minutes until the crust is deep golden in patches and the bread sounds hollow when tapped on the base. Eat while the crust is still crackling.

attrs.problem: Bread flat and dense without a hollow interior
attrs.avoid: Avoid under-rising or baking the bread at a temperature lower than the maximum your oven can reach.
attrs.fix: The very high heat is what causes the rapid steam expansion that creates the hollow. A lower oven gives a dense, bready result. Preheat for a full 30 minutes and use the hottest setting available.

attrs.problem: Ends shrink back and the canoe shape disappears during baking
attrs.avoid: Avoid leaving gaps between shaping and baking; the dough relaxes quickly at this hydration level.
attrs.fix: Bake the shaped shoti within 30 minutes of shaping. Twist and pinch the ends firmly; they should be taut, not just pinched lightly.
